# GameInfo <Badge type="info" text="class" />

<p class="api-meta">Namespace <code>Lustral</code> · Assembly <code>Lustral.Api</code></p>

Information about the running game, as reported by the game itself. Lustral reads it from the game's files before any mod loads.

```csharp
public sealed class GameInfo
```

## Properties

### Backend {#backend}

```csharp
public ScriptingBackend Backend { get; }
```

The game's scripting backend.

### Developer {#developer}

```csharp
public string? Developer { get; }
```

The game's developer (`Application.companyName`), or null if not set.

### Directory {#directory}

```csharp
public string Directory { get; }
```

The absolute path of the game's folder, which contains its executable.

### Name {#name}

```csharp
public string Name { get; }
```

The game's name (`Application.productName`), for example `Lethal Company`.

### UnityVersion {#unityversion}

```csharp
public string? UnityVersion { get; }
```

The Unity version the game was built with, for example `2022.3.62f2`, or null if unknown.

### Version {#version}

```csharp
public string? Version { get; }
```

The game's version (`Application.version`), for example `1.2.0`. Some games display a different version to players. Null if Lustral cannot read the version from the game's files, which can occur with Unity versions newer than Lustral supports; the version is then read once the game is running (by [`Mod.OnGameReady`](/api/mod#ongameready)) and stored for subsequent launches.
